text: The three days of travel may be read as a kind of suspended sentence; outwardly nothing happens in them, and yet everything of consequence is happening. Obedience and horror go side by side through the whole journey, and the narrator lets neither prevail over the other. Faith in this story has little of feeling in it; it is an arrangement of fixed relations, like a geometry. Its points are set down plainly. The narrator dwells upon the servants, the wood, the knife, and the fire, and so names the instruments of the act before Abraham comes to the act itself.
